Abstract:

This research work focuses on the current advances and challenges in 3D face reconstruc tion and recognition, with special attention given to the limitations associated with the use of low-cost consumer-grade sensors in healthcare, security, and real time robotic applica tions. By systematically reviewing multiple notable works, the domain is categorized into: (i) 3D face reconstruction and mesh recovery via monocular algorithms (ii) multi-view and sensor-based 3D reconstruction (iii) low-cost and real-time face recognition systems and (iv) various data augmentation, alignment and occlusion handling strategies. This work ex plores the transition from traditional statistical methods and manual descriptors to modern neural network frameworks designed to handle the noise and structural deficiencies present in the depth data. We analyze how these frameworks balance geometric precision with human-robot interaction. Furthermore, based on the identified challenges faced during real time robotic deployment- in terms of environmental sensitivity, demographic inclusivity, data variation, and computational trade-off- this work defines a set of targeted research objectives. These proposed objectives provide a strategic roadmap for the development of resilient and lightweight biometric systems in specialized environments.
